claims.text: Refractory HEAs alloyed with titanium will exhibit improved low-activation properties.
Refractory HEAs alloyed with zirconium will exhibit improved low-activation properties.
Titanium- and zirconium-alloyed refractory HEAs are suitable for high-temperature plasma-facing components in fusion reactors.
The proposed material will operate in high-temperature fusion-reactor environments under neutron irradiation.
Microstructural stability mediates the effects of titanium and zirconium alloying.
Phase composition mediates the effects of titanium and zirconium alloying.
Adding titanium and zirconium enhances the thermal stability of refractory HEAs.
Adding titanium and zirconium reduces the neutron-induced activation of refractory HEAs.
Enhanced thermal stability and reduced activation improve alloy performance under neutron irradiation.
Titanium- and zirconium-alloyed refractory HEAs will have lower post-irradiation activation than refractory HEAs without those additions.
Titanium- and zirconium-alloyed refractory HEAs will have improved high-temperature mechanical properties relative to refractory HEAs without those additions.
The magnitude of the improvements depends on the specific alloy composition.
The magnitude of the improvements depends on processing methods.
